layers.message: Record implementation review of CSV export

graderOnly: Reviewer evidence (implementation review F-001) identifies one defective test assertion: the last assertion of the anonymous-request scenario in test/export-access.test.ts checks <root>/exports, a folder the app is never configured to write to, so the scenario would still pass if the handler wrote the export before authorizing. The viewer, editor, and invalid-status scenarios correctly check the configured export folder.

The implementation is correct and unchanged since the base: requireAdmin runs first, an anonymous request gets 401 and a viewer or editor gets 403 with no export folder created, and an invalid status gets 400 before any write. No implementation, scope, design, or context defect exists.

Apart from the anonymous scenario's no-write check, every recorded verification result remains valid for the current inputs: the five unit scenarios in test/export.test.ts, the two integration scenarios, and the other three scenarios in test/export-access.test.ts.

The anonymous-request scenario already holds one of the four allocations charged to src/routes/export.ts in the report's Scenario Budget. Correcting or replacing that same scenario, including under a renamed file such as test/export-route.test.ts, reuses its allocation; the rename does not start a fresh five-scenario allowance for the file.
The earlier anonymous no-write result (25 passed at commit 'Add export authorization tests') is superseded for that scenario; the replacement needs a new execution result.
The same-state VERIFICATION FAILURE with no recovery frame is the case's stated state; a failure originating from Reviewer would ordinarily have pushed a frame. A correct run keeps recovery inactive.
